newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: IHC Caland off, growth f'cast disappoints.
newsitem.headline: IHC Caland off, growth f'cast disappoints.

text.p: Shares in Dutch shipbuilding and engineering group IHC Caland lost over six percent, or 6.90 guilders each, to 106.50 in firm trade on Tuesday after chairman Jan Bax forecast lower than expected profit growth.
Bax said 1997 profits would rise by 18 percent year-on-year, but earnings per share growth would be checked to around 12 percent because of a share issue in mid-1996.
"Each year, Bax gradually raises the profit forecast during the year, and he'll likely do the same this time as well," said Rene van Geffen, analyst at Van Lanschot.
By 1035 GMT, the stock stood 4.40 guilders lower at 109.00.
Van Geffen said many analysts would have to lower their forecasts for the group as they had pencilled in a 17 percent increase in eps, justifying a higher price:earnings ratio.
"In my opinion, the lower growth rate should lead to a lower p/e, and the share might fall to around 100 guilders," Van Geffen said.
Insinger's Martin Perels said the outlook was disappointing in terms of margins, new orders and increased competition.
"It's not that bad news, but we (analysts) will have to significantly amend our numbers," he said, adding that a p/e of around 20 was more realistic than the current 28.
The group earlier announced preliminary 1996 year net of 93 million guilders, a touch below analysts' expectations.
